articles.title: Save $40 Off Microsoft's Professional-Grade Xbox Elite Series 2 Core Wireless Controller
articles.body:
Do you prefer PlayStation or Xbox controllers? I'm in the latter camp. My favorite PC controllers have always been modeled after Xbox's tried and true asymmetrical layout. And when it comes to Xbox controllers, you can't get much better than the highest end model from Microsoft itself. For a limited time, Amazon is offering the professional-grade Xbox Series X Elite Series 2 Core Wireless Controller for $109.99 with free shipping. It's currently $150 everywhere else.

Xbox Elite Core Wireless Controller for $109.99

Xbox Elite Series 2 Core Wireless Controller

The Elite Series 2 Core is the official premium controller for Xbox. The Core model is physically identical to the previous generation $200 Xbox Elite Series 2 controller, with integrated pro gaming features like adjustable-tension thumbsticks, wrap-around rubberized grip, and shorter hair trigger locks. The only difference is that the original Elite controller comes with more accessories: extra sets of paddles, thumbsticks, D-pad, and a travel case. The Elite Series 2 Core doesn't come with any of those accessories. You can buy them separately as a component pack for $59.99.

The price drop may be a precursor the Series 3 release

IGN's Jacqueline Thomas reported on rumored leaks that the Elite Series 3 release might be on the horizon. I'm not very optimistic, however, that the launch price will be the same as the Xbox Series 2 controller when it first released at $179.99. Given that the price of the Elite Series 2 with component pack is $200, I expect the same price or higher.

articles.title: The Batman Part 2 Brings in Director Steven Soderbergh to Finish Film in Place of Matt Reeves
articles.summary: Ocean's 11 director Steven Soderbergh has been hired to finish filming The Batman Part 2 while Matt Reeves attends to a family matter.
articles.body:
UPDATE: Matt Reeves has released his own statement, confirming that he is still very much apart of the film's produciton and is not leaving the project.

"Just to be clear, I am not leaving The Batman Part II," said Reeves . "I am profoundly grateful to Steven for coming to my aid during this challenging time to help me finish principal photography. Thank you to all for your concern and well wishes."

Ocean's 11 director Steven Soderbergh has been hired to finish filming The Batman Part II while Matt Reeves attends to a family matter.

It was reported earlier this month that The Batman Part II director Matt Reeves was abruptly stepping away from the project to attend to personal matters. This left the film in a strange state of limbo, but DC boss Peter Safran recently told IGN that the project would be finished . Now we know how. Warner Bros. confirmed to Deadline that Ocean's 11 director Steven Soderbergh will helm and complete the superhero sequel during its final weeks of production.

“As Matt Reeves continues to attend to an ongoing family matter, Steven Soderbergh, as an admirer of Matt’s work, approached Matt and will step in to help the writer-director complete the final weeks of principal photography on The Batman Part II," a WB rep told Deadline. "Matt and Steven will work closely together with the actors and crew to fulfill Matt’s vision of the film.”

The Batman: Part II - Who's Who in Matt Reeves' DC Sequel

Soderbergh is working directly with Matt Reeves during this process, with Deadline reporter Justin Kroll noting that Reeves is working on the film remotely from his home. Once the movie is wrapped, Soderbergh will hand things back over to Reeves so he can handle the post-production process. The goal is to finish Reeves' original vision for the sequel as opposed to having Soderbergh do something radically different.

“I thought Matt Reeves’ work on The Batman was stunning; it was intentional, specific, and rigorously coherent," said Soderbergh. "The goal here is to work with Matt and his team to generate footage that will integrate seamlessly with what’s already been shot so Matt can properly finish his film.”

As of right now, it's unclear if the stoppage will lead to another delay. The Batman Part II has already been pushed back several times and is currently due out February 2028 . Given it's expected that there isn't too much left to shoot on the movie, this may not create any significant setbacks.

Soderbergh is a pretty efficent director, often handling multiple production roles himself. He's known for having a firm handle on budgets and being able to shoot quickly, which is something that the studio will likely greatly appreciate in this situation. He also has an Oscar for Best Director, which gives him an extra degree of prestige.

The Batman Part II is currently slated to hit theaters on February 18, 2028.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: The Fourth Wing TV Series Has Reportedly Found Its Xaden and Violet
articles.summary: Prime Video's adaptation of the best-selling romantasy series, Fourth Wing, has reportdely found its stars. Esther McGregor has been cast as Violet Sorrengail and Emilio Sakraya will be taking on the role of Zaden Riorson.
articles.body:
Prime Video's adaptation of the best-selling romantasy series , Fourth Wing, has reportdely found its stars. Esther McGregor has been cast as Violet Sorrengail and Emilio Sakraya will be taking on the role of Zaden Riorson.

The news arrived earlier today via Deadline stating that the two actors have been confirmed. This is the first casting news we've received about the highly anticipated adaptation, and it's the most impactful. The heart of Rebecca Yarros' steamy fantasy romance series is the relationship between these two characters, so their performance will make or break the series.

Prime Video has found its leading stars for ‘Fourth Wing,’ the TV series adaptation of Rebecca Yarros’ bestselling novel. Esther McGregor has been cast as Violet Sorrengail, and Emilio Sakraya will bring to life the character of Xaden Riorson, sources close to production tell Deadline. More details here: — Deadline (@DEADLINE) October 15, 2026

Prime Video has found its leading stars for ‘Fourth Wing,’ the TV series adaptation of Rebecca Yarros’ bestselling novel. Esther McGregor has been cast as Violet Sorrengail, and Emilio Sakraya will bring to life the character of Xaden Riorson, sources close to production tell Deadline. More details here:

You may know Esther McGregor for her role as Isabel in A24's Baby Girl , where she worked alongside Nicole Kidman and Antonio Banderas. She also appeared in an episode of Obi-Wan Kenobi as Tetha Grig, a pink-haired spice dealer, which is notable because she is in fact Ewan McGregor's daughter.

Emilio Sakraya is perhaps most well-known for his depiction of ex-con Giwar Hajabi in the 2022 film Rheingold. You may also know him from his stint as JC in the first season of Netflix's Warrior Nun series .

For those not already familiar with the Fourth Wing books (AKA the Empyrean series), let's quickly break down who these characters are: Violet Sorrengail is the main protagonist in the books and is often referenced as a beautiful but frail girl with a deadly side to her. Xaden Riorsen is portrayed as a dark, powerful, and misunderstood guy with too many secrets. Both of these characters attend Basgiath War College where they learn to control powers given to them by massive dragons.

Whether or not these actors can accurately portray these two characters remains to be seen, but they definitely appear to fit their book descriptions. Seeing as this is the most important relationship in the series, they will need to have very good chemistry to be able to portray the love/hate relationship that makes the first Fourth Wing book so good.

The Fourth Wing TV series does not currently have a release date attached, but we do already know that Meredith Averill is serving as showrunner and executive producer. Rebecca Yarros will also be an executive producer on the project alongside Michael B. Jordan's Outlier Society.

While fans are waiting for the TV adaptation to become a reality, Rebecca Yarros is currently working on book four of the series. She's also been collaborating on several tabletop adaptations for the franchise as popularity continues to grow. Most recently, Yarros released Threshing Day , a standalone novel depicting the perspectives of various other characters on the day they got their dragons.

Jacob Kienlen is a Senior Audience Development Strategist and Writer for IGN. Born and raised in Portland, Oregon, he has considered the Northwest his home for his entire life. With a bachelor's degree in communication and 10 years of professional writing experience, his expertise is spread across a variety of different pop culture topics — from TV series to books and the latest LEGO sets .

articles.title: Remedy Boss Reacts After Control Resonant Sells 1 Million Copies, Becoming Studio's Fastest-Selling Game
articles.summary: Control Resonant has sold one million copies, becoming Remedy’s fastest-selling game in spite of leakers cracking the title and pirating it after its digital launch in September.
articles.body:
Control Resonant has sold one million copies, becoming Remedy’s fastest-selling game in spite of leakers cracking the title and pirating it after its digital launch in September.

Remedy celebrated this milestone on October 15, writing on Twitter/X, “Thank you for the support. For playing, sharing, and being a part of the community.”

Remedy’s communications director Thomas Puha also commented on this achievement, saying, “There we go. Strong start.”

There we go. Strong start. — Thomas Puha (@RiotRMD) October 15, 2026

This means that Control Resonant has soared past Alan Wake 2 , which previously held the record for the studio’s fastest-selling title. The legacy sequel reached one million copies sold two months after its release; Control Resonant has achieved that figure in just three weeks.

This is welcome news for both Remedy and fans of the game, many of whom urged players against downloading the pirated version of the title when it launched digitally in late September. It seems this wasn’t a crippling setback for the developer, though, given its current financial success — and physical editions of the game have just now been released, so there’s still more profit to be had.

Control Resonant was met with critical acclaim among both reviewers and players alike. We at IGN scored it an eight out of 10 , with reviewer Michael Higham saying, “Even when combat's sharp edge eventually dulls, Control Resonant is a great addition to the Remedyverse. While its story follows a more standard framework, its gravitational pull is in the inventive world built around it and the humanization that grounds the paranatural intrigue.”

In fact, the game was so good that many internet pirates decided against illegally downloading it, choosing instead to support Remedy in the hopes that its success would help keep the studio alive.

"One of the very few games I'm going to be buying, Remedy are on the brink of bankruptcy, this is their make or break title, I love their games and gotta do what I can to keep them afloat," wrote one fan on a piracy subreddit.

"I wasn't planning to buy it but now I feel like I should," another said. "I like Remedy. They do good games."

Remedy is known for titles like the original Control game, Alan Wake 2, Max Payne , and Quantum Break . And while their offerings have been met with high praise from players, they aren’t necessarily tailored for mass appeal, leaving some gamers worried about the developer’s future — but if these latest figures are anything to go by, it seems to be faring just fine.

Virginia (she/her) is IGN’s News Editor. With ten years of experience reporting on games and entertainment, she’s got a storied background in the fighting game community, influencer news, and viral online trends. Find her on Twitter at @TheeMissGlaze .

articles.title: Does the Vision Feel Abandoned by the Avengers? ‘I Think So,’ Says Paul Bettany
articles.summary: VisionQuest stars Paul Bettany and James Spader on the father-son dynamic behind the new MCU series, the lack of Avengers, Ultron's feelings about Wanda, and more.
articles.body:
It’s been almost five years since we last saw the Vision in WandaVision, but now he’s back – or a version of him is, anyway – in the new Disney+ series VisionQuest . Paul Bettany returns as the android (synthezoid for you Marvel heads) alongside James Spader’s Ultron and a variety of other AIs from the MCU, including JARVIS (James D'Arcy), FRIDAY (Orla Brady), and EDITH (Emily Hampshire).

But you know who’s not present for the new show? Wanda Maximoff or the Avengers. That doesn’t come as much of a surprise considering that Wanda (Elizabeth Olsen) is, well, dead after the events of Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness , and the Avengers just aren’t themselves these days, what with there apparently being two teams floating around the MCU right now (which none of the original members are a part of).

Notably, in the VisionQuest premiere, Vision muses to himself about how he seems to have evaded everyone who’s been looking for him since the events of WandaVision. “There isn’t an enemy, an acquaintance… or even an Avenger trying to find the Vision,” he says. But when he says this line, Bettany delivers it with a sort of melancholy realization. So of course I had to ask the actor about it when we spoke recently – specifically if Vision feels abandoned by the Avengers in that moment.

“Well, I think so,” Bettany explains. “I finally realized that I was really making Vision for a version of me as a child, where I felt like the outsider who was bullied. I didn't think I would ever fit in anywhere. So it's just a moment to remind [us]... It's sitting on a chair at a dance, a school dance, you know what I mean? And having the courage to go and talk to a girl.”

And then there’s the Wanda of it all. Somehow I doubt there’s a single Marvel fan out there who thinks the Scarlet Witch is really, truly dead, despite the whole Mount Wundagore falling on top of her thing in Doctor Strange 2. At this point in the series, Vision (formerly known as White Vision, who lacked the emotions and memories of the original Vision before meeting a magical version of the OG back in WandaVision – it was a whole thing) is detached from humanity, as well as any deep feelings about Wanda (or at least that’s how he’s presenting). But how about Ultron, the now-imprisoned villain who Wanda and her late brother Pietro (Aaron Taylor-Johnson) once worked for? What are his thoughts on the Vision’s former partner and the mother of their children?

“He's pretty rude about Wanda,” Spader tells me. Essentially, Wanda is dead now, and so for Ultron she doesn’t matter anymore. “Ultron lives in the present. He really lives in the present. And he's ready to step forward. And he's not going to step forward until he shoves [Vision] ahead of him.”

Regarding the relationship between Vision and Ultron, while when we first meet him here, Ultron is trapped in the artificial reality that Vision has constructed, the two clearly have an important bond. “He's sort of like a quasi-therapist, psychotic father figure,” Bettany says of Spader’s character.

“I think without question, he looks at him as a son-like figure,” says Spader. “It serves him well to perceive him as that. ... But I think the more interesting thing is how much it matters to him how Vision perceives him. And it's touching in a way because he … allows himself to not care or to appear to not care, but he does. He really does care. But what's interesting is it's not so much he cares how he feels about Vision. It's he really cares about how Vision perceives him.”

Fans will recall the great scene between Vision and Ultron from Avengers: Age of Ultron, where the two synthetic lifeforms discussed humanity – both the pros and the cons of the species. It was that scene – which Spader points out was actually filmed in a parking lot and not a forest as it appears to be in the final film – which really is a key to why Ultron is back for VisionQuest, and what the relationship between the two characters is all about.

“It's this little seed of the last scene with them in Age of Ultron,” says Spader. “[We] grew it and watered it and fed it and raised it and gave it light and it blossomed into this amazing show and story. And these characters, they came from this seed, but they grow into this fabulous thing, this fabulous creation [that's] funny and moving and sad and tragic and incredibly exciting and thrilling and disturbing at times.”

In that scene from 11 years ago, Vision says the following to the defeated Ultron:

“Humans are odd. They think order and chaos are somehow opposites, and try to control what won't be. But there is grace in their failings. I think you missed that.”

Says Spader, “He spends 13 years really embracing that idea and really embracing humanity because of that idea. Where it's him. He is chaos. That's what he is. That's what he lives for. That's who he is. And yet his son is dedicated at this present time to trying to find order and trying to process this. And what they then learn from one another is fabulous and funny and exciting and challenging for both of them. And they both get as much from each other as the other.”

The actors also think that there’s been a shift of perspective for Vision since Age of Ultron in that the events since that film – when Viz was, don’t forget, just born yesterday – have caused the android to have “very real doubts” and be confused by the chaos of the world, and more specifically, the chaos that humanity brings.

“But it's funny, the two of them are very different,” continues Spader. “Vision has a sense of consequences and has a sense of collateral effect that I don't think Ultron... Ultron just wants more. And I don't think he thinks about the consequences. I think he accepts chaos in all its forms and therefore … the dichotomy between their two reactions, and how it comes together, they force it together.”

VisionQuest is streaming on Disney+ now.

Talk to Scott Collura @scottcollura.bsky.social , or listen to his Star Trek podcast, Transporter Room 3 . Or do both!

articles.title: Rep. Ritchie Torres Introduces Legislation to Ensure Gamers Own Their Digital Games
articles.summary: Democratic Congressman Ritchie Torres is introducing legislation that aims to ensure you own your digital games, rather than having a license.
articles.body:
Democratic Congressman Ritchie Torres is introducing legislation that aims to ensure you own your digital games, rather than merely buying a license that gives you permission to play them.

The bill, known as The Power to the Players Act, would direct the Fedral Trade Commission (FTC) to establish regulations that would protect gamers and their digital libraries. In short, Torres wants to ensure that when you buy a digital game, you actually own it, as opposed to getting a license that can be revoked. Additionally, the bill would require online games to have offline functionality, so that when servers are shut down, the content can still be played by those who own the game.

“Consumers must have the right to own, the right to play, and the right to transfer the games they buy,” Torres said in a press release . “A game that can be taken away the moment a company pulls the plug is not a purchase. It is a rental disguised as a sale. Families in the Bronx and across the country save up to buy these games, and they deserve better than a license that can vanish at any time. The Power To The Players Act ensures consumers own what they buy and can keep playing long after a company moves on.”

Torres made an example out of NBA 2K25, a game that recently announced that it would be rendering single-player modes inaccessible due to servers shutting down. The news gained widespread attention, as many were confused why a game that's only two years old was becoming obsolete so soon.

Torres' bill addresses ongoing controversies in the industry. Earlier this year, it was confirmed that PlayStation would be ditching physical games starting in 2028 , which would mean gamers wouldn't be able to truly own their games starting with the next-generation. GTA 6 is also skipping a physical release this November , meaning there won't be any used copies of the game following its release. It's a slippery slope, and one that gamers have been battling for some time now.

The Stop Killing Games movement has been fighting to make games more accessible to their current owners, even after they shut down servers. Torress' bill would ensure they get their way, at least in the United States. Of course, we'll have to see if this bill makes it to the finish line, but it's a noble effort and shows that someone is trying to make change happen.

Cade Onder is a freelancer for IGN's news team. He covers all things entertainment, including gaming, film, and more. You can find him on Twitter @Cade_Onder.

articles.title: Save $900 Off the New 2026 65" Hisense UR8 RGB Mini-LED TV, One of the Best TVs You Can Get for Gaming
articles.summary: The new 2026 RGB Mini-LED tech boasts richer colors, a brighter picture, and wider viewing angles than ever before.
articles.body:
Last year, Hisense pioneered the first RGB Mini-LED TV with its 116UX model. Granted it was only available as a massive 116" screen that retailed for $20,000. In 2026, Hisense released its second generation RGB Mini-LED tech at a much more affordable price point with its UR-series lineup. Ahead of Black Friday, you can get it for even less. Best Buy has just discounted the 65" Hisense UR8 RGB Mini-LED TV from $2,000 all the way down to $1,099.99 with free shipping.

The Hisense UR8 RGB Mini-LED TV Gives OLED a Run for Its Money

RGB Mini-LED is essentially the next generation evolution of Mini-LED technology. Traditional mini-LED TVs consist of an array of blue LED that are passed through RGB filters to produced the desired color. RGB Mini-LED TVs use red, green, and blue LEDs instead of just blue, which means the pixels no longer need filters to produce the desired color. The result is more accurate color reproduction, less blooming and, most importantly, a wider color gamut. In fact, the color gamut of RGB Mini-LED surpasses that of OLEDs, since current-generation OLEDs also use color filters combined with blue OLEDs. How does that translate in the real world? It means that you see richer, more accurate colors, smoother gradients and less banding than even OLEDs, especially in 4K HDR content.

RGB Mini-LED TVs have several other features that out-class standard Mini-LEDs. They're brighter (far brighter than OLED TVs), making them perfect for daytime watching in bright rooms with little light control. They offer much better viewing angles, which means everyone you're hosting will enjoy the game wherever they're positioned around the TV. Gamers will benefit from this TV as well. The Hisense UR8 boasts a 180Hz native refresh rate, the highest I've ever seen for a TV, with HDMI 2.1 inputs that will pair seamlessly with a PlayStation 5 console for seamlessly running games in 4K.

articles.title: Allisha Gray injury update: Dream All-Star remains 'day-to-day' ahead of WNBA Finals
articles.summary: The availability of Atlanta Dream All-Star guard Allisha Gray is up in the air ahead of Game 1 of the 2026 WNBA Finals against the Golden State Valkyries.
articles.body:
The availability of Atlanta Dream All-Star guard Allisha Gray is up in the air ahead of Game 1 of the 2026 WNBA Finals against the Golden State Valkyries .

Following practice on Thursday, Oct. 15, Gray said she remains "day-to-day" with a left hand injury that she suffered in Game 1 of the Dream's semifinal series win over the New York Liberty on Oct. 4. The four-time All-Star said she's trending in the right direction after undergoing a minor procedure on her injured hand, but the Dream's medical team will have the final say on whether or not she suits up for Saturday's contest.

"Progress has been great, so we're heading in the right direction," Gray told reporters. "Just more so relying on the medical staff. They'll know what's best for me... So it's just taking it day by day, just me getting comfortable, being able to handle the physicality of practice and stuff, which has been feeling well."

The 6-foot guard was a limited participant in Thursday's practice in San Francisco. She participated in shooting drills with black tape holding her left ring finger and pinky finger together. She also appeared to have a bandaid on her left middle finger.

"As long as I can shoot, I'm good," Gray added. "Hopefully I get some good news where I am able to play Saturday."

Liberty, Dream and Aces, Valkyries in WNBA semifinal playoff action

Gray suffered the left hand injury in Game 1 of the Dream's WNBA playoff semifinals series against the New York Liberty on Sunday, Oct. 4. Gray first exited the game holding her left wrist and hand area with 3:59 remaining in the first quarter before returning to the bench at the 9:09 mark of the second quarter with her ring finger and pinky taped. With 3:44 remaining in the first half, Gray dove for a loose ball and appeared to injure the same hand. She left the game and was ruled out before halftime.

"I actually injured it on the first (play)," Gray clarified on Thursday. "Me coming back out was just my competitive nature of not wanting to sit out, but it was just a point where I couldn't play anymore, so I knew that I wasn't able to help my tear anymore, so it was best for me to sit down."

The injury kept Gray out of Game 2 and Game 3 of the semifinal series over the Liberty, which the Dream swept to punch their ticket to the WNBA Finals for the first time since 2013.

On Tuesday, Gray revealed she underwent a "minor procedure" on her left hand. Although she didn't disclose the specific procedure, or when she had it, Gray said "everything is put together and fixed. I'm good to go."

The Dream eagerly await the return of Gray, who is averaging 17 points and 1.7 rebounds across three postseason games.

"If we just swept New York with no (Allisha Gray), just imagine what it's going to be like when we bring her back and she's got extra rest," Rhyne Howard said. "She's got an extra week of rest under her belt. The shot's looking good, so it shouldn't be no question about that. But I think once we bring her back, then it's going to be even more unstoppable for us."

Dream guard Allisha Gray is "day-to-day" with a left hand injury.

At the 3:59 mark of the first quarter in Game 1 of a semifinal playoff series, Gray exited holding her left wrist and hand area. Gray was down on the floor for a few moments before being helped up. She went to the locker room for several minutes before returning to the bench at the 9:09 mark of the second quarter. Gray checked back in at the 8:30 mark of the second quarter with two fingers taped (her ring and pinky) on her left hand. She attempted a field goal but missed it. Once she missed the shot, she took off her tape.

Just before halftime, at the 3:44 mark, Gray was diving for a loose basketball on the floor, trying to secure a possession for Atlanta, when she appeared to injure the same hand again. Gray sat on the court, cradling her hand/fingers before going back to the locker room for a second time.

Gray was later ruled out with a left hand injury just before halftime. She returned to the bench after being ruled out, with her left hand heavily wrapped around her ring and pinky fingers. Within the wrap, Gray had a splint on her ring finger.
authors: Cydney Henderson and Meghan L. Hall, USA TODAY

articles.title: Save 34% Off the Storied Klipsch ProMedia 2.1 Lumina Computer Speakers Well Ahead of Black Friday
articles.body:
I'm sure many of us older PC gamers are familiar with the venerable Klipsch ProMedia 2.1 computer speakers. They were, frankly, without equal for a better part of two decades. I owned them during the majority of my college life and used them up until I had kids. Although there were incremental updates throughout the years, a complete redesign didn't happen until late 2025 in the guise of the Klipsch ProMedia Lumina 2.1 . It launched at a steep price tag of $379.99, but today you can get it on Amazon for just $249.99 with free shipping after a hefty 34% off instant discount.

34% Off the New Klipsch ProMedia Lumina 2.1 PC Speakers

Klipsch ProMedia Lumina 2.1 Computer Speakers

The new Klipsch Promedia Lumina looks very different from its predecessor. Design-wise, the Luminas feature a two-tone black and silver facade with wood-grain wrap throughout. It looks sophisticated and would fit well even in a non-gaming setup. The Lumina features RGB lighting, but it's subtle and projects toward the wall behind of your desk.

The 2.1 channel form factor remains unchanged. The satellite speaker is a touch bigger than before and features a 3" mid-range driver and a 1” mylar tweeter mated to a Microtractrix horn. The subwoofer is much slimmer and features a ported design with a 6.5" side-firing woofer.

Plenty of quality-of-life upgrades have been made to the Lumina, including a USB Type-C connection to your PC, wireless Bluetooth 5.3 connectivity, and a Klipsch Control desktop app that allows you to tweak EQ and lighting from your PC.

I haven't actually tried these speakers out myself, but at this price I'm tempted. I'm currently using a pair of Audioengine speakers and although they are quite good, they take up a lot of space on my desk and I don't have a discrete subwoofer.
